paper: Afzal et al., The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Search for Signals from New Physics, ApJL 951, L11 (2023), arXiv:2306.16219
target: Table 4 (longtable tab:list): Bayes estimators, maximum posterior values and 68% credible intervals for every new-physics model, in both the NP and NP+SMBHB analyses

data.licence: CC-BY-4.0, no login and no click-through

frozen_rule.estimator: The paper defines it, which is why this target was chosen. Appendix A: the Bayes estimator is the expectation value of the 1D marginal and the standard deviation is the square root of its variance, computed in practice as the sample mean and sample standard deviation of the MCMC chain. We compute exactly that, unweighted, over the samples as deposited.
frozen_rule.chain_handling: Primary reading uses each chain as deposited, with nothing discarded and no thinning, because the deposit is described as the chains that were analysed. If the deposit turns out to carry an explicit burn-in column or a documented convention, we follow it and say so.
frozen_rule.tolerance: Table 4 prints two decimals. A claim reproduces when our value rounds to the printed one, that is when the absolute difference is below 0.005. Differences between 0.005 and 0.05 are reported as near misses rather than failures, since MCMC sampling noise of a mean is real.

secondary_readings_declared_in_advance.burn_in: the same statistics after discarding the first 25% of each chain, to show whether the printed values depend on that choice
secondary_readings_declared_in_advance.maximum_posterior: the mode of the 1D marginal needs a density estimate, which the paper does not specify. We use a Gaussian KDE with Silverman bandwidth on the same samples, and report the bandwidth sensitivity rather than scoring the cell as a failure.
secondary_readings_declared_in_advance.ci68: the equal-tailed 16th-84th percentile interval, and the highest-density interval, both reported; the paper does not say which it printed

out_of_scope.bayes_factors: The Bayes factors between models, including the 10 to 100 range favouring several cosmological models over SMBHBs, come from the evidence and not from the marginals. Recovering them means rerunning the inference, which is not what a chain recount can do.
out_of_scope.k_bound: the K ratio of Eq. (10) is a likelihood ratio, not a property of the marginal
out_of_scope.caveat: recounting from the authors own chains checks the summarising step, not the inference behind it
